title: Cowrite comment event
description: One line of a `.cowrite/comments/<doc-hash>/<author>.jsonl` append-only event log (TD-4). Thread state is the causal fold of these events (test-plan P5): `create` starts a new thread whose id *is* this event's own `id`; `reply`/`revise`/`withdraw`/`resolve`/`reopen`/`re_anchor`/`address`/`link_changes`/`decide_linked_change` act on the thread named (transitively, via `parent_id`) by the event that `parent_id` references. `revise` and `withdraw` directly target the comment or reply named by `parent_id` and only apply when `author` matches that target's author (D24). `publish` directly names a root comment in `parent_id` and records that it reached an external review audience (D20/J10); the publication fact survives later withdrawal. `parent_id` is absent/null only for `create`. `address`/`address_stopped`/`address_failed`/`link_changes`/`decide_linked_change` (P2a-19, FR-CMT-2/7; `address_stopped`/`address_failed` added by issue #1381) are the "Address with AI" pending/conclusion/delivery/decision events: `address` starts a run (`addressed — pending review`), and — since issue #1778 — carries `started`, whether *this event itself* is genuine per-thread start evidence (`true` for the single-thread path; `false` for a batch's own per-thread dispatch, which cannot observe real per-thread progress yet) — absent on events written before this field existed, which always meant `true`; `address_stopped`/`address_failed` conclude a run that ended without delivering (stopped by the user, failed/crashed, or reconciled as failed because no live run answers to it any more) — each matched against its named pending run without clearing another, a no-op otherwise; `link_changes` lands its tracked-change delivery; `decide_linked_change` records a linked change's accept/reject outcome, which drives whether the thread auto-resolves or reopens. An unrecognized `type` value is forward-compatible by design (P5: unknown event types are skipped by the fold, not rejected) — this schema only checks the envelope fields for it, matching the drift tolerance of `docs/formats/provider-contract`'s stream-event schemas.

id.description: Globally unique, minted by the writer (UUID/ULID). For `create`, this id *is* the thread id.

parent_id.description: The thread-or-reply this event acts on. Only null for `create`.

timestamp.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, stamped by the author's own clock. Cross-machine clock skew is expected — folds order by (timestamp, id) with buffer-until-parent, never by file-arrival order.

run_id.description: The Address run whose defense this reply delivers. Older replies omit this field and remain readable; a legacy defense can clear pending state only when exactly one run is pending.

published.description: FR-CMT-4/D20: publish-to-external-reviewer flag for a defense reply. Absent on events written before P2a-19; a reader defaults it to false, matching the Rust writer's `#[serde(default)]`.

parent_id.description: Root comment id whose publication to a review audience is recorded (D20/J10).

guidance.description: The [Try again — add guidance…] re-delegation note; null/absent for a first address.

started.description: Issue #1778: whether this event itself is genuine per-thread start evidence, as opposed to merely targeting the thread. `true` for the single-thread path (dispatch and start are the same event); `false` for a batch's own per-thread dispatch fallback. Absent on events written before this field existed — a reader defaults it to `true`, matching the Rust writer's `#[serde(default = "address_started_default")]`.

run_id.description: The `address` run this stop concludes — matched against the thread's current pending run; a stale id (superseded by a later re-delegation) is a no-op.
The `address` run this failure concludes (a CLI/spawn/read failure, or a load-time reconciliation of a marker with no live run) — same matching as `address_stopped`.

change_ids.description: Tracked-change ids (`propose_changes`/P2a-13's `change_set`'s member ids) this delivery links to the thread.

anchor.$comment: TD-4's shared anchor shape, as persisted in sidecar files (includes base_revision). The simpler agent-facing anchor an MCP tool call supplies — no base_revision, since the agent doesn't mint one — is `provider-contract/mcp-tool-call.schema.json`'s `$defs.anchor`.
